summary: Hive-Pal is a mobile-first application designed for apiary management, allowing you to record inspections, track queen lifecycles, and monitor equipment inventories directly from the field. It provides a streamlined interface tailored for quick data entry while working outdoors with hives. Built with Node.js and distributed under the MIT licence, it is intended to be self-hosted via Docker.
goodFor: It suits small-scale beekeepers or hobbyists who want to keep their livestock and equipment records on a private server rather than relying on third-party cloud services.
watchOut: With a modest community following and a steady but cautious maintenance profile, you may encounter edge cases or lack integration with wider agricultural platforms. You will also need to handle your own mobile synchronisation and backup routines.
deployNotes: As a containerised Node.js application, deployment typically requires mounting a persistent volume for your database and configuration files, alongside a reverse proxy to handle HTTPS termination for secure mobile access.
